entry.description: Lenses make many points: pure point spectrum disproves Simon’s L² conjecture. The primary source reports: For every d>=2 and0<=sigma<1/3, the authors construct a smooth bounded nonnegative potential V with arbitrarily small ||V||_infinity+integral |x|^(1−d+sigma)|V|², for which −Delta+V has only pure point spectrum on(0,infinity). This contradicts Simon’s stated weighted-L² absolutely-continuous-spectrum conjecture. Direct AI connection: Becker and Yang describe developing the initial construction with ChatGPT, which supplied the point-spectrum parameter adjustment, spectral averaging and extension from a bounded interval to the full positive spectrum; humans rewrote and checked the argument. Further checking: Independently check the lens and higher-dimensional construction, weighted norm, spectral averaging and the exact positive-energy meaning. Human responsibility and rewriting are not independent end-to-end proof verification. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Retain provisional=1, low strict confidence, taxonomy unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

Further checking: Audit tightness, centering, uniqueness of the limiting law, SHF measurability and non-Gaussianity, including the failed intermediate strategies described in AppendixC. Do not extend Gaussian-polymer hypotheses to an unrestricted universality theorem. No downloaded proof artifact was executed.
